channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Brainard Pitches $1,000 Down Payments For First-Time Homebuyers
item.description: Lael Brainard, former vice chair of the Federal Reserve, said there is 'no reason for the Fed not to hike' rates in December after core CPI from October exceeded estimates. Brainard, who also served as the director of the National Economic Council During the Biden Administration, discussed her proposal for a program that would allow to $1,000 down payments for qualified first-time homebuyers as she said potential buyers struggle to gather the larger sum required for a traditional down payment. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hegseth Impeachment Effort Sets 'Horrible Precedent,' Says Rep. Troy Downing
item.description: Republican Representative Troy Downing said the Hegseth impeachment effort in Congress sets a 'horrible precedent that’s going to disable any administration in the White House moving forward' and said that in his opinion Hegseth's actions do not rise to level of 'high crimes and misdemeanors.' Downing declined to reveal who he would back to lead Republicans in the House, but said that it is important that the leader 'combats crazy' coming from House Democrats. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Democrats Can Combat Trump’s Global Chaos
item.description: Trump has destroyed America’s relationships with its global allies, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Andreas Kluth says. Now that the Democrats have taken the House and the Senate, this is what they can do to stop him from going further. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: GOP Taps Combative Jordan as Next House Minority Leader
item.description: House Republicans elected hardline Ohio Representative Jim Jordan to be the party’s leader in the next Congress, choosing a new face to lead it in the wake of the worst midterm electoral drubbing in half a century.
item.dc:creator: Erik Wasson and Maeve Sheehey

item.title: UK Arrests US Army Soldier Over Russia Spying Allegations
item.description: British police have arrested a US Army soldier on suspicion of being involved in a Russian espionage operation in a case that involved both UK and American authorities.
item.dc:creator: Iain Marlow and Joe Mayes

item.title: Major Blockchains Have Not Been Hacked: Securitize CEO
item.description: Kristin Smith, interim CEO of the Blockchain Association, and president of the Solana Policy Institute, joins Isabelle Lee and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." With Democrats set to control Congress following their midterm sweep, the industry faces the prospect of tougher rules and closer scrutiny of its ties to President Trump. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Securitize CEO Talks Earnings, Binance Hack, Tokenization
item.description: Carlos Domingo, chairman, co-founder, and CEO of Securitize, joins Isabelle Lee and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." They discuss the company's earnings results, the fallout from the US midterms, tokenization, and Binance hack. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Disclosure: “The Government Knew She Was Not a Spy”
item.description: Decades after their parents were executed by the US for espionage conspiracy, the government released documents that Robert and Michael Meeropol say show that their mother wasn’t a spy — and that the government knew it. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Iran Producing 50 Missiles Per Month Despite Crippled Industry
item.description: A western intelligence estimate says Iran can build about 50 ballistic missiles per month — roughly half its prewar capacity — providing a formidable means of retaliation if hostilities resume, despite months of airstrikes.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Palasciano, Gerry Doyle and Golnar Motevalli

item.title: Sanders Won’t Back Schumer for Senate Majority Leader Job
item.description: Sen. Bernie Sanders won’t support Sen. Chuck Schumer’s bid to lead Senate Democrats next year, he told reporters Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Zach C. Cohen

item.title: Congress Has to Support Municipal Bonds Says Brock
item.description: Through October, municipal issuers have sold $511 billon of municipal bonds in 2026, up 4% from 2025, which puts the market on pace for a third consecutive record high, and the market could surpass $600 billion for the first time. Bloomberg Intelligence spoke with Emily Brock, Director of the Federal Liaison Center for the Government Finance Officers Association to discuss how state and local governments build public support for their infrastructure investments and Bond Programs on-site at BAM Mutual. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Burnham Rejects EU Financial Rules Showing Brexit Reset’s Limits
item.description: Andy Burnham’s government won’t accept so-called dynamic alignment of the UK’s financial services rules with those of the European Union, a stance that raises questions about the premier’s wider ambitions for closer ties.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham and Alberto Nardelli

item.title: Hegseth Calls Massie Impeachment Bid an Attack on Troops
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, speaking at the Pentagon, addressed the impeachment effort against him in Congress, casting the move as a politicized attack on US troops and lawful military operations ordered by President Donald Trump. The House is scheduled to begin procedural votes on the impeachment resolution Tuesday evening. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fed's Logan Calls For at Least Two More Rate Hikes
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas President Lorie Logan says the pace of interest rate hikes needs to speed up. During a speech in Houston on Tuesday, Logan said “it remains clear to me, given the current outlook, that the FOMC needs to implement at least two more 25-basis-point rate increases." Bloomberg's Enda Curran reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: White House CEA Chair Says Fed Rate Hike Is Premature
item.description: White House Council of Economic Advisers Chairman Chris Phelan admits the October CPI report was "not a good number," and inflation came in hot. But he still says raising interest rates by 50 basis points would be premature. He speaks on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: IBM to End Immigration Sponsorship for Roles in Biggest Unit
item.description: International Business Machines Corp. is ending immigration sponsorship for some roles in its largest division following a crackdown by the Trump administration on a visa program that’s been a talent pipeline for the tech industry.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford and Alicia A. Caldwell

item.title: Hegseth Says Impeachment Bid Amounts to ‘Sabotage’
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth mounted a combative defense against the impeachment effort against him in Congress, casting the move as a politicized attack on US troops and lawful military operations ordered by President Trump. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rubio Touts Productive Ukraine Talks and Need to Include Europe
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio touted a productive first day of US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine to end their war, now in its fifth year, saying that President Donald Trump’s administration and Europe have the same goals in mind.
item.dc:creator: Eric Martin and Ania Nussbaum

item.title: Top Biden Economist Pitches $1,000 Down for First-Time Buyers
item.description: A top Biden administration economic official is pitching Democrats on a low-down-payment proposal to bring millions of new homebuyers into the market, as incoming congressional leaders take stock of affordability measures that might help them notch early legislative wins.
item.dc:creator: Katy O'Donnell

item.title: WuXi AppTec Taken Off Pentagon’s Chinese Military Firms List
item.description: WuXi AppTec Co. has been removed from the US government’s list of Chinese military companies, giving the contract research organization that’s relied on by global drugmakers at least a temporary reprieve from restrictions and reputational damage tied to the designation.
item.dc:creator: Amber Tong
